A randomized controlled trial compared the efficacy of azithromycin versus doxycycline/ciprofloxacin for the syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections in resource-limited settings. (Rustomjee R, Kharsany AB, Connolly CA, Karim SS. J Antimicrob Chemother. 2002;49(5):875-8.) 2. An audit was conducted on the use of benzathine penicillin, post-treatment syphilis serology, and partner notification in patients with early infectious syphilis. (Chauhan M, Serisha B, Sankar KN, Pattman RS, Schmid ML. Int J STD AIDS. 2006;17(3):200-2.) 3. A study evaluated the acceptability and compliance of daily procaine penicillin injections in the outpatient treatment of syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum. (Crow G, Theodore C, Forster GE, Goh BT. Sex Transm Dis. 1997;24(3):127-30.) 4. An audit reviewed the management of early syphilis at North Manchester General Hospital. (Kingston MA, Higgins SP. Int J STD AIDS. 2004;15(5):352-4.) 5. A retrospective analysis of early syphilis management was conducted in Teesside, covering the years 2005–2007. (Tayal S, Ahmed MS, Hanif U. Int J STD AIDS. 2009;20(9):647-9.) 6. A systematic review examined the prevalence and utilization of healthcare services for reproductive tract infections and sexually transmitted infections in India. (Nagarkar A, Mhaskar P. Indian J Sex Transm Dis. 2015;36(1):18-25.) 7. An overview of systematic reviews explored interventions aimed at improving the safe and effective use of medicines by consumers. (Ryan R, Santesso N, Lowe D, Hill S, Grimshaw J, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2014;4:CD007768.) 8. A qualitative study investigated women’s perspectives on choosing and using sexual health services. (Dixon-Woods M, Stokes T, Young B, Phelps K, Windridge K, Shukla R. Sex Transm Infect. 2001;77(5):335-9.) 9. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report on global surveillance of sexually transmitted infections in 2015, highlighting trends and challenges. (WHO, Geneva, 2016.) 10. The emergence of multidrug-resistant, extensively drug-resistant, and untreatable gonorrhea has been documented, posing significant public health concerns. (Unemo M, Nicholas RA. Future Microbiol. 2012;7:1401-22.) 11. Verified treatment failures with cefixime for gonorrhea have been reported in Norway, England, and other countries, raising concerns about resistance. (Unemo M, Golparian D, Syversen G, et al. Euro Surveill. 2010;15(47):pii:19721.) 12. High-level resistance to cefixime and ceftriaxone in Neisseria gonorrhoeae has been identified in France, Japan, and Spain, linked to novel genetic mutations. (Unemo M, Golparian D, Nicholas R, et al. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2012;56(3):1273-80.) 13. Azithromycin resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae has been reported globally, with high-level resistance documented in Sweden, Japan, and other regions. (Unemo M, Golparian D, Hellmark B. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2014;58(1):624-5.) 14. Treatment failures with azithromycin and cefixime have been observed in England, Canada, and Australia, indicating co-evolution of resistance mechanisms. (Allen VG, Seah C, Martin I, et al. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2014;58(5):2528-34.) 15. Studies on gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum have evaluated single-dose therapies with kanamycin, ceftriaxone, and cefotaxime, demonstrating varying levels of efficacy. (Fransen L, Nsanze H, D’Costa L, et al. Lancet. 1984;2(8414):1234-7.) 16. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses have assessed the effectiveness of prophylactic agents, such as erythromycin and silver nitrate, in preventing neonatal conjunctivitis caused by gonorrhea and chlamydia. (Darling EK, McDonald H. J Midwifery Womens Health. 2010;55(4):319-27.) 17. Cost-effectiveness analyses have been conducted on community-based interventions, such as the Chlamydia Monday program in Sweden, to reduce STI prevalence. (Deogan CL, Bocangel MK, Wamala SP, Månsdotter AM. Scand J Public Health. 2010;38(2):141-50.) 18. The WHO guidelines for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae emphasize the importance of addressing antimicrobial resistance and optimizing treatment regimens. (WHO, Geneva, 2016.) 19. High-level azithromycin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains have been identified in Ireland, France, and Argentina, raising concerns about the efficacy of dual-antimicrobial regimens. (Lynagh Y, Mac Aogáin M, Walsh A, et al. J Antimicrob Chemother. 2015;70(8):2411-3.) 20. Studies on neonatal gonococcal conjunctivitis have highlighted the effectiveness of single-dose ceftriaxone and cefotaxime, as well as the need for improved prophylactic measures. (Laga M, Naamara W, Brunham RC, et al. N Engl J Med. 1986;315(22):1382-5.
